version.value: Orchestral movement with wordless women’s chorus; performing edition unestablished
version.note: Research-only, unpublished candidate. No listening file, timed annotations, orchestra map or score-alignment claim is supplied because the chorus cannot be fully identified. Neither instrumental movement’s authorship resolves this distinct performer requirement.

performers.note: PERFORMER-BLOCKED: the orchestra and conductor are documented, but this list is deliberately incomplete and is not a publishable credit. The required full identity of the women’s chorus remains unestablished. IA names only OSR/Ansermet and contains no LP label image. Stuart S080 identifies orchestra/conductor but no chorus. Decca/Eloquence’s official 1951 reissue page omits a choir name. CiNii’s matching POCL-4628 / 466 217-2 catalogue record says only “Female Chorus”. The specialist comparison explicitly calls the 1951 ensemble “Ein ungenannter Frauenchor” (an unnamed women’s chorus). No full institutional or ensemble name can responsibly be substituted. The user’s skip-unnamed-performers rule therefore blocks publication.

date.note: Month/year established; exact day unknown. Stuart’s dated 10th and 12th entries refer to Prokofiev items [c] and [d], not Nocturnes [a].

place.note: The venue does not establish that an unnamed chorus was a particular Geneva or OSR-associated ensemble.

catalogue.note: First UK issue March 1952, not 1951. Stuart also gives London LL 530, June 1952. No source label image was available in the IA file list.

matrixTakeSides.value: Side A, third movement; suite master series SAR587–SAR592
matrixTakeSides.note: The six masters are assigned to Nocturnes as a suite, not to individual movements here. Exact Sirènes matrix, take and LP runout are unestablished.

credits.note: Digital-transfer credit absent. Victor Olof, producer, and Gil Went, engineer, belong to the original recording session and are not credited with this upload’s transfer.

composition.value: Public-domain underlying composition under ordinary life-plus-70 terms
composition.note: Debussy died in 1918 and the original Nocturnes publication dates to 1900–01. This is separate from recording and edition rights.

recording.value: Rule 3 territorial pre-1963 publication basis; US public-domain status not established; publication separately blocked by performer identity
recording.note: March 1952 LXT 2637 publication is before the project’s 1963 threshold. The ordinary former EU 50-year sound-recording term would have expired before the 1 November 2013 extension threshold. This territorial basis is not a worldwide licence, and US status remains unestablished. No IA open-licence URL is supplied. Establishing this rights basis does not waive the unresolved-chorus publication block.

rights.creditLine: UNPUBLISHED CANDIDATE — Debussy, Sirènes from Nocturnes; Orchestre de la Suisse Romande, Ernest Ansermet; women’s chorus identity unresolved. Recorded October 1951, Victoria Hall, Geneva; Decca LXT 2637, issued March 1952. Internet Archive transfer credit unknown. Territorial Rule 3 basis only; US public-domain status not established.
